A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

1) 25.2%, or 32 of 127, of NF1 mutations induce aberrant splicing; 2) 40.6%, or 13 of 32, of these aberrant splicing errors were due to exonic variants; 3) 1 of the 127 mutations produced mosaicism; and 4) computational analyses were able to predict the underlying mechanism of the aberrant splicing caused by 29 of 127 NF1 variants.
